name: js-yaml-timestamp-dropped-by-core-schema-puppy-lib
behavioral_change: js-yaml 5.0.0 made the YAML 1.2 `CORE_SCHEMA` the default schema of `load()`; this schema lacks the YAML 1.1 `!!timestamp` tag, so a scalar such as `date: 2001-01-23` is returned as the string `'2001-01-23'` instead of a JavaScript `Date`. The function name, arity and call form are unchanged and no error or warning is raised.
downstream_effect: The downstream project (puppy-lib) loads every data file in `src/data` with `yaml.load` and exposes the result on `site.data`; after the upgrade the `date` field of the invoice fixture becomes a string and the checked-in ava snapshot no longer matches. The only location in the output is `test/index.mjs:30:5`; `lib/context.js`, js-yaml, schema and timestamp are never mentioned.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes one line in `lib/context.js` (line 63), calling `yaml.load(file.contents.toString(), { schema: yaml.YAML11_SCHEMA })`.
documented_in: The js-yaml v4 to v5 migration guide (https://github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/5.2.3/docs/migrate_v4_to_v5.md), section Schema, states that legacy YAML 1.1 types such as `!!timestamp` require `YAML11_SCHEMA` and shows `load(source, { schema: YAML11_SCHEMA })`; the 5.0.0 CHANGELOG also declares the change. Tier 1: the documentation shows the new code form.
failing_tests: test/index.mjs :: vinyl files are annotated with puppy site and page data
